matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Soil contains many kinds of living organisms. Bacteria and fungi help break down organic matter and cycle nutrients.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Some fungi help roots take up nutrients. Worm channels can help water and air enter soil.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Fungi tse ding di thusa metso ho monya dimatlafatsi. Meselana e entsweng ke diboko e ka thusa metsi le moya ho kena mobung.

matchingFields.proposedFullText: Sheba metso, sebopeho sa mobu le motsamao wa metsi, hammoho le dintho tse phelang mobung tse bonahalang.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Put soil and water in a clear jar, with a little suitable dispersing detergent. Close and shake it, then leave it undisturbed.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Kenya mobu le metsi ka clear jar, o kenye hanyenyane ya suitable dispersing detergent. E kwale mme o e sisinye, ebe o e siya e sa sisinyehe.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Sand settles first. Silt settles next, while clay can remain suspended much longer.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Sand e dula fatshe pele. Silt e latela, athe clay e ka nna ya dula e suspended nako e telele haholo.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: This is a rough learning exercise. Clumps and unsettled clay can mislead you; use a soil laboratory when accurate texture is needed.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Ena ke rough learning exercise feela. Dikgobokano tsa mobu (clumps) le clay e so duleng fatshe di ka o kgelosa; sebedisa soil laboratory ha o hloka soil texture e nepahetseng.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: A thick sand layer beneath cloudy water does not yet tell you the final proportions. Some fine particles may still be suspended.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Lera le letenya la sand ka tlasa cloudy water ha le eso o bolelle final proportions. Fine particles tse ding di ka nna tsa dula di suspended.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Compare the settled layers and feel the soil in the field.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Bapisa likarolo tse lutseng, ’me u utloe mobu tšimong.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Record what you see and what remains uncertain. Do not prescribe watering or soil treatments from one jar alone.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Ngola seo u se bonang le seo u sa kholisehang ka sona. U se ke ua etsa qeto ea ho nosetsa kapa ho alafa mobu ka lebaka la nkho e le ’ngoe feela.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Compaction, poor drainage and loss of organic matter can limit roots and soil life.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Ho thatafala ha mobu (compaction), drainage e mpe le tahlehelo ya organic matter di ka sitisa metso le bophelo ba mobu.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Pale colour or few worms do not prove that chemicals killed the soil. Worm activity also changes with moisture and season.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Mmala o lerootho kapa palo e nyane ya diboko ha e pake hore dikhemikhale di bolaile mobu. Mosebetsi wa diboko le wona o a fetoha ho latela mongobo le sehla.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Look for patterns across the field. Check management history, drainage and plant growth before choosing a remedy.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Batla mekhoa e iphetang tšimong. Hlahloba nalane ea tsamaiso, metsi a phallang le kholo ea limela pele u khetha tharollo.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Compost is organic matter broken down under managed conditions.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Compost ke organic matter e qhaqhollwang ka tsela e laolwang.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Finished compost can improve soil structure and contribute nutrients.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Compost e phethilweng e ka ntlafatsa sebopeho sa mobu mme ya fana ka dimatlafatsi.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Time to readiness varies with materials, moisture, air and temperature. A province name or a fixed number of weeks is not a readiness test.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Nako ya hore compost e lokele ho sebediswa e fapana ho ya ka materials, mongobo, moya le thempereitjha. Lebitso la province kapa palo e behilweng ya dibeke ha se readiness test.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Mix dry browns with fresh greens. Avoid thick, wet layers that keep air out.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Kopanya dry browns le fresh greens. Qoba layers tse teteaneng, tse metsi tse thibelang moya ho kena.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: If the heap becomes slimy or smells strongly of ammonia, add dry browns and turn it.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Ha qubu ya compost e ka ba slimy kapa e nkha ammonia haholo, eketsa dry browns mme o e phethole.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Check moisture and air as the heap changes; one recipe does not suit every mix of materials.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Hlahloba mongobo le moya ha qubu ya compost e ntse e fetoha; recipe e le nngwe ha e tshwanele motswako o mong le o mong wa materials.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: A hot centre does not prove that every part of a heap has been treated. Time, temperature and management all matter.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Karolo e bohareng e tjhesang ya qubu ha e pake hore karolo e nngwe le e nngwe ya yona e se e treated. Nako, temperature le management kaofela di bohlokwa.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Keep meat, dairy, diseased plants, pet waste and contaminated materials out of this simple household system.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Boloka meat, dairy, diseased plants, pet waste le contaminated materials di le ka ntle ho tsamaiso ena e bonolo ya lapeng.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Do not assume home composting destroys every weed seed or disease organism. Use a recognised process where sanitation is required.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: U se ke ua nahana hore home composting e fedisa peo e nngwe le e nngwe ya mofoka kapa disease organism e nngwe le e nngwe. Sebedisa recognised process moo sanitation e hlokahalang.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Keep wattle seed pods out of the compost heap. An ordinary heap may not make every seed non-viable.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Boloka wattle seed pods di le ka ntle ho qubu ya compost. Qubu e tlwaelehileng e ka nna ya se etse hore peo e nngwe le e nngwe e be non-viable.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Use only clean, untreated materials. Bark breaks down slowly; its name alone is not proof that it is free of contamination.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Sebedisa materials tse hlwekileng feela, tse sa alafwang. Bark e bola butle; lebitso la yona feela ha le pake hore ha e na contamination.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Check the heap and turn when it needs more air or mixing. Keep it moist rather than waterlogged.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Hlahloba qubu ya compost mme o e phethole ha e hloka moya o mongata kapa ho kopanngwa. E boloke e le mongobo, e se ke ya ba waterlogged.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Cover bare soil with suitable clean mulch, such as straw, dry grass or wood chips.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Koahela mobu o pepesitsweng ka mulch e hlwekileng e loketseng, jwalo ka straw, dry grass kapa wood chips.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Mulch can reduce evaporation, soften the impact of rain and suppress weeds.

currentTarget.text: Mulch e ka fokotsa evaporation, ya fokotsa matla ao pula e otlang mobu ka wona, hape ya fokotsa mefoka.

matchingFields.proposedFullText: Mulch e ka fokotsa evaporation, ya fokotsa matla ao pula e otlang mobu ka ona, mme ya fokotsa kgolo ya mefoka.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Keep it clear of trunks and stems. Check moisture underneath and adjust the layer; more mulch is not always better.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: E boloke e le hole le trunks and stems. Hlahloba mongobo ka tlasa mulch mme o fetole layer ha ho hlokahala; mulch e ngata ha e dule e le betere.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Cover crops can protect ground between main crops. Choose for local weather, available water and the next planting.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Cover crops di ka sireletsa mobu pakeng tsa main crops. Di kgethe ho latela boemo ba lehodimo ba sebakeng sa heno, metsi a fumanehang le next planting.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: The course examples include oats, lupins, sunn hemp and cowpea. Check local suitability before sowing.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Mehlala ya thuto ena e kenyelletsa oats, lupins, sunn hemp le cowpea. Hlahloba hore di loketse sebaka sa heno pele o jala.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Legumes need suitable bacteria and growing conditions to fix nitrogen. Nutrients in their residues become available as the material decomposes.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Legumes di hloka bacteria tse loketseng le maemo a kgolo a loketseng hore di kgone ho fix nitrogen. Dimatlafatsi tse masalleng a tsona di a fumaneha ha thepa eo e ntse e bola.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Worm farms can turn suitable food scraps and bedding into castings. Check the bin rather than expecting a fixed harvest date.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Worm farms di ka fetola food scraps le bedding tse loketseng hore e be worm castings. Hlahloba bin ho e-na le ho lebella letsatsi le behilweng la kotulo.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin is called leachate. It is not the same as a prepared worm-casting tea.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin e bitswa leachate. Ha o tshwane le worm-casting tea e lokisitsweng.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Leachate can contain harmful organisms or substances. Do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Leachate e ka ba le harmful organisms kapa substances. O se ke wa e sebedisa hodima edible plants kapa wa nahana hore ho e hlapolla ho etsa hore e bolokehe.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: A Highveld field left bare after the maize harvest faces two main risks.

currentTarget.text: Tshimo ya Highveld e siilweng e sa kwahelwa ka mora kotulo ya maize e tobana le dikotsi tse pedi tse kgolo.

matchingFields.proposedFullText: Tšimo ea Highveld e siiloeng e sa koaheloa ka mor’a kotulo ea maize e tobana le likotsi tse peli tse kholo.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Winter wind can carry away dry topsoil.

currentTarget.text: Moya wa mariha o ka fefola topsoil e ommeng wa e tlosa.

matchingFields.proposedFullText: Moea oa mariha o ka nka mobu o ommeng o ka holimo.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: The first heavy spring storm can strike bare ground and damage its surface and structure. If water runs over the field, it can carry loosened soil away.

currentTarget.text: Sefefo sa pele se matla sa selemo se ka otla mobu o sa kwahelwang, sa senya bokahodimo le sebopeho sa wona. Ha metsi a phalla a feta tshimong, a ka nka mobu o hlephileng a o tlosa.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Finished compost can improve soil structure and contribute nutrients.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Finished compost yi nga antswisa xivumbeko xa misava ni ku contribute nutrients.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Time to readiness varies with materials, moisture, air and temperature. A province name or a fixed number of weeks is not a readiness test.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Nkarhi wo lungheka wa hambana hi materials, moisture, air na temperature. Vito ra province kumbe nhlayo leyi vekiweke ya mavhiki a hi readiness test.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Mix dry browns with fresh greens. Avoid thick, wet layers that keep air out.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Hlanganisa dry browns na fresh greens. Papalata thick, wet layers leti sivelaka air ku nghena.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: If the heap becomes slimy or smells strongly of ammonia, add dry browns and turn it.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Loko heap yi va slimy kumbe yi nun'hwa ammonia swinene, engetela dry browns kutani u yi turn.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Check moisture and air as the heap changes; one recipe does not suit every mix of materials.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Kambela moisture na air loko heap yi ri karhi yi cinca; recipe yin'we a yi ringani eka nkatsakanyo wun'wana ni wun'wana wa materials.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: A hot centre does not prove that every part of a heap has been treated. Time, temperature and management all matter.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Hot centre ya heap a yi tiyisisi leswaku every part ya heap yi treated. Time, temperature and management all matter.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Keep meat, dairy, diseased plants, pet waste and contaminated materials out of this simple household system.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Hlayisani meat, dairy, diseased plants, pet waste na contaminated materials swi ri ehandle ka simple household system.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Do not assume home composting destroys every weed seed or disease organism. Use a recognised process where sanitation is required.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: U nga teki leswaku home composting yi lovisa weed seed yin'wana ni yin'wana kumbe disease organism yin'wana ni yin'wana. Tirhisa recognised process laha sanitation yi lavekaka.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Keep wattle seed pods out of the compost heap. An ordinary heap may not make every seed non-viable.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Hlayisani wattle seed pods ehandle ka compost heap. An ordinary heap may not make every seed non-viable.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Use only clean, untreated materials. Bark breaks down slowly; its name alone is not proof that it is free of contamination.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Tirhisa clean, untreated materials ntsena. Bark breaks down slowly; vito ra yona ntsena a hi vumbhoni bya leswaku a yi na contamination.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Check the heap and turn when it needs more air or mixing. Keep it moist rather than waterlogged.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Kambela heap kutani u yi turn loko yi lava air yo tala kumbe mixing. Yi hlayise yi ri moist, ku nga ri waterlogged.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Cover bare soil with suitable clean mulch, such as straw, dry grass or wood chips.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Funengetani misava leyi nga hava cover hi mulch leyi basekile, leyi faneleke, yo fana na straw, byanyi byo oma kumbe wood chips.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Mulch can reduce evaporation, soften the impact of rain and suppress weeds.

currentTarget.text: Mulch yi nga hunguta evaporation, yi olovisa ku ba ka mpfula naswona yi hunguta nhova.

matchingFields.proposedFullText: Mulch yi nga hunguta evaporation; yi nga olovisa ku ba ka mpfula naswona yi nga suppress weeds.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Keep it clear of trunks and stems. Check moisture underneath and adjust the layer; more mulch is not always better.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Keep it clear of trunks and stems. Kambelani moisture ehansi ka yona, mi lulamisa layer; mulch yo tala a yi vuli leswaku swi ta antswa nkarhi wun'wana ni wun'wana.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Cover crops can protect ground between main crops. Choose for local weather, available water and the next planting.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Cover crops ti nga sirhelela misava leyi nga kona between main crops. Ti hlawuleni hi ku ya hi weather ya laha, mati lama kumekaka ni next planting.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: The course examples include oats, lupins, sunn hemp and cowpea. Check local suitability before sowing.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Swikombiso swa course swi katsa oats, lupins, sunn hemp na cowpea. Kambelani loko swi fanele ndhawu ya kwalaho mi nga si swi byala.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Legumes need suitable bacteria and growing conditions to fix nitrogen. Nutrients in their residues become available as the material decomposes.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Legumes ti lava bacteria leti faneleke ni suitable growing conditions leswaku ti fix nitrogen. Nutrients leti nga eka masalela ya tona ta kumeka loko material yi ri karhi yi bola.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Worm farms can turn suitable food scraps and bedding into castings. Check the bin rather than expecting a fixed harvest date.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Worm farms ti nga hundzuluxa food scraps ni bedding leswi faneleke swi va castings. Kambelani bin ematshan'weni yo langutela fixed harvest date.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin is called leachate. It is not the same as a prepared worm-casting tea.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin yi vuriwa leachate. A yi fani na prepared worm-casting tea.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Leachate can contain harmful organisms or substances. Do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe.
matchingFields.proposedFullText: Leachate yi nga va na harmful organisms kumbe substances. Do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: A Highveld field left bare after the maize harvest faces two main risks.

currentTarget.text: Nsimu ya le Highveld leyi siyiweke yi nga pfaleriwangi endzhaku ka ntshovelo wa maize yi langutane ni makhombo mambirhi lamakulu.

matchingFields.proposedFullText: Nsimu ya Highveld leyi tshikiweke yi nga funengetiwangi endzhaku ka ntshovelo wa maize yi langutana ni makhombo mambirhi lamakulu.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Winter wind can carry away dry topsoil.

currentTarget.text: Moya wa xixika wu nga rhwala topsoil leyi omeke wu yi susa.

matchingFields.proposedFullText: Mheho wa xixika wu nga susa misava ya le henhla leyi omeke.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: The first heavy spring storm can strike bare ground and damage its surface and structure. If water runs over the field, it can carry loosened soil away.

currentTarget.text: Storm ya ximun’wana yo tika yo sungula yi nga ba misava leyi nga pfaleriwangi, yi onha vuandlalo ni xivumbeko xa yona. Loko mati ma khuluka ehenhla ka nsimu, ma nga rhwala misava leyi ntshunxekeke ma yi susa.

matchingFields.proposedFullText: Xidzedze xo sungula xo tika xa ximun’wana xi nga hlasela misava leyi nga funengetiwangi, xi onha vuandlalo ni xivumbeko xa yona. Loko mati ma khuluka ehenhla ka nsimu, ma nga teka misava leyi ntshunxekeke ma famba na yona.

matchingFields.sourceEnglish: Cover crops, mulch, and organic matter can help hold soil in place and help it stay alive.

currentTarget.text: Cover crops, mulch na organic matter swi nga pfuna ku khoma misava yi nga susiwi ni ku yi pfuna yi hambeta yi hanya.

matchingFields.proposedFullText: Cover crops, mulch ni organic matter swi nga pfuna ku khoma misava endhawini ya yona ni ku yi pfuna leswaku yi ya mahlweni yi hanya.
